clue.text: Dance musician — one trying to hit all the pitches?

definitions.text: one trying to hit all the pitches?

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
a musician is a player of an instrument

explanation.surface: A dance-band instrumentalist who aims to sound every note accurately.
explanation.walkthrough: The pitches look like musical notes, but they are the throws a baseball batter faces; the question mark flags the playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of a baseball batter, who swings at what the pitcher throws.

clue.text: Knowing millions must be lost on parade

indicators.note: says the letter for millions has to be dropped from the word for parade

parts.note: a parade is a march

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that a fortune is being wasted on a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be lost on' removes M from MARCH. 'Knowing' reads as a verb in the surface but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a playfully sly, mischievous look can be called either.

clue.text: Gift handkerchief now available, with tons shifted up front

indicators.note: says the letter for tons moves from its place at the end to the very start

parts.note: hanky is the informal word for a handkerchief
a book or record that is out is now available

explanation.surface: A shop has presentation hankies in stock, with heaps moved to the window display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted up front' takes the T ending HANKY OUT and puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, it is a small present given to show gratitude.

clue.text: Being thrifty using mat found in river

indicators.note: says the mat sits inside the letters of the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England
a rug is a mat

explanation.surface: A penny-pincher makes do with a carpet fished out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The mat is not fished out of any water: 'found in' is a container signal, and the river is a Cornish one beloved of setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone economical and sparing with money is described by both.

clue.text: Feeling sick after question missed out is simple

indicators.note: says the letters for question are left off the word for feeling sick

parts.note: queasy means feeling sick

explanation.surface: An exam candidate feels ill after skipping a question that was actually straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed out' drops QU from QUEASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a task needing little effort is both.

clue.text: Wait for dispatch from lazy morning official

parts.note: a lie-in is a morning spent staying late in bed
state as an adjective means official, as in a state visit

explanation.surface: Hang on for a message sent by an idle civil servant on the early shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The dispatch is not a message: it is the sending-off of a dead dignitary whose body is displayed before the funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a dead ruler's body rests on public view until the burial sends it off.

clue.text: Activity of bruisers cost union terribly

indicators.note: badly or dreadfully, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Thuggish behaviour by heavies has been ruinously expensive for the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges COST UNION. The bruisers are not thugs but blows that leave marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, it is the medical term for the mark a blow produces on skin.

clue.text: Lament university opening up only part of the day

indicators.note: the university letter splits open the word for part of the day and sits inside

parts.note: morn, the morning, is just one part of the day

explanation.surface: People regret that the college opens for just a few hours daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening up' puts U inside MORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both verbs mean to grieve over a loss.

clue.text: Affected person gets parking fees returned

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for fees is read from its end to its start

parts.note: dues are fees owed

explanation.surface: Someone hit by a charge gets car-park money given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' means pretentious, not harmed, and 'returned' is a turnaround signal rather than money handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a pretentious poser, someone putting on intellectual airs.

clue.text: Right in displaying cheek rash

indicators.note: says the letter for right goes inside the word for displaying cheek

parts.note: someone impudent is showing cheek, or insolence

explanation.surface: A patient is correct to show the doctor a skin complaint on the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside IMPUDENT. 'rash' is the adjective meaning reckless, not a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe acting without thought for the consequences.

clue.text: Disorderly pub not shut — one might ring time?

indicators.note: unruly and out of order, so the letters of the three words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy bar is still open, though someone may call last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' rearranges PUB NOT SHUT. In British pubs 'time' is called, often with a bell, at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical example: pressing such a control could sound a bell or a timer.

clue.text: Gelatin substitute made from head of African fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A setting agent is produced from the top end of a fish caught off Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a seaweed jelly cooks use as a vegetarian setting agent.

clue.text: Promenade engulfed by highest rollers

indicators.note: swallowed up, so the letters lie inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A seafront walkway is swamped by the tallest waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfed by' marks letters running across 'highest rollers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean a leisurely walk, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Try to justify men banning new dance

parts.note: to excuse something is to try to justify it

indicators.note: to ban is to shut out, so the letter for new is removed from the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to defend the men who outlawed a modern dance craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' takes N out of MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a ballroom number in which anyone may cut in and take another's partner.

clue.text: Mostly offensively coarse nonsense

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: crude means offensively coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Rubbish talk that is, for the most part, vulgar and rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of CRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both mean rubbish or worthless talk.

clue.text: How to describe Christmas where we are

definitions.meaning: 25 December is the date on which gifts are exchanged
the current time, the point in history we now occupy

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is a date for gifts, and as an adjective it means current or contemporary.

clue.text: Grassland flower flatter around the top of calyx

indicators.note: says the word for flatter goes round the letter picked from calyx

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A meadow bloom spreads lower and wider near the upper part of its sepals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like a comparative adjective but is a verb, and 'around' makes its two-word synonym a container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a yellow wild bloom common in meadows.

clue.text: Trouble over one offspring's secret affair

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is an offspring

explanation.surface: There is a row about a child's clandestine romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AIL into LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an illicit romantic relationship.

clue.text: Rude to a silly government supporter?

indicators.note: rough and unrefined, so the letters of the three words after it are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is impolite to a foolish backer of the ruling party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude' rearranges TO A SILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one who stays faithful to the established rulers, notably in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: I don't know opera lover's reason for living in New York

definitions.meaning: what you say when a question stumps you

definitions.text: opera lover's reason for living in New York
definitions.meaning: moving one space in the last two words makes a remark to a New Yorker that the city has the Met, its famous opera house

explanation.surface: An opera fan cannot explain why they live in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: shift the T across the last word break and the phrase says the Metropolitan Opera is in this city.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom admitting you are stumped, which respaced boasts of a local opera house.

clue.text: Embarrassed about amusing cash repayment

indicators.note: says the word for embarrassed goes round the word for amusing

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
fun as an adjective means amusing, as in a fun evening

explanation.surface: Someone is sheepish over a comical instance of paying money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amusing' is an adjective here, matched by a noun used adjectivally; 'about' is a container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money handed back to a customer.

clue.text: What young gangster grows to full maturity?

definitions.meaning: a hood is a gangster, so a juvenile one ends up as a grown-up one
the state of being fully grown

explanation.definitionFit: The grown-up state, which split in two names a mature mobster.

clue.text: Tea party host chasing constant gossip

indicators.note: the host follows after the constant, so the constant comes first

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
the Hatter hosts the mad tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: The person giving an afternoon tea is forever after tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' places HATTER after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: idle talk, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Kindling brush with old trick once it's set up

parts.note: to brush against something is to touch it lightly

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: to do someone is to trick or swindle them

explanation.surface: A close encounter with a familiar con, after the fire has been laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once it's set up' turns DO into OD at the foot of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is dry decayed timber used as tinder to start a fire.

clue.text: Infamy of short Labour slogan? Tony is gutted

indicators.note: cut short, so the imagined slogan loses its final letter

parts.note: a whimsical chant for Britain's Labour Party, whose rivals are the Tories (Conservatives)

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A brief party catchphrase brings disgrace, and Tony is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the S from NO TORIES; 'is gutted' leaves TY from Tony. Tony evokes Blair, the former Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the state of being well known for something bad.

clue.text: Staggering range shown by revolutionary grape variety

indicators.note: lurching unsteadily, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: Che Guevara is crosswords' stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A radical new kind of grape shows an astonishing spread of flavours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' rearranges RANGE into GRENA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a red wine vine widely grown in southern France and Spain.

clue.text: Club follows spades having come out in bursts

indicators.note: the club comes after the spades letter, so that letter leads

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: In a card game a club is played after spades, which had appeared in flurries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' places PUTTER after S. The club is a golf club, not a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to emerge in spitting, explosive spurts, as words or an engine do.

clue.text: Heed gag on suffering academic

indicators.note: in distress and out of shape, so the letters of the two words before it are disturbed

explanation.surface: Take note of the silencing order imposed on a persecuted professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges HEED GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal label for a highly intellectual, bookish person.

clue.text: Exercise that goes from both ceiling and floor

indicators.text: that goes from both ceiling and floor
indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same starting at the top or at the bottom

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A workout move that can start at the top of the room or the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that goes from both ceiling and floor' says the down entry reads identically downwards and upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a gym movement in which you haul your chin to a bar.
